skills/toil/dynatrace.md

Monitored entities, services, Kubernetes workloads and problems from the Dynatrace Environment API v2, and distributed-trace spans from Grail. Every command reads; none changes anything. Verification level: unit.

Supported versions: The oldest Dynatrace version toil supports hasn’t been established. The classic commands call Environment API v2 (/api/v2) on SaaS and Managed; trace needs the platform Grail query API (/platform/storage/query/v1), so a deployment without the platform can’t run it. No release has been verified yet.

Credential

Two hosts, two tokens, and each token goes only to its own host:

  • Access token, for every command except trace. In Dynatrace: Access tokens → Generate new token, with the entities.read and problems.read scopes. toil sends it to baseUrl as Authorization: Api-Token <token>.
  • Platform token, for trace only, with the storage:spans:read and storage:buckets:read scopes. toil sends it to platformUrl as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

There is no username, password or browser login, and no CI fallback variable.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_DYNATRACE_BASE_URLfor all but traceClassic environment URL, like https://<environment-id>.live.dynatrace.com. On Managed, keep the /e/<environment-id> path
apiTokenTOIL_DYNATRACE_API_TOKENfor all but traceAccess token, sent as Api-Token
platformUrlTOIL_DYNATRACE_PLATFORM_URLfor tracePlatform URL, like https://<environment-id>.apps.dynatrace.com
platformTokenTOIL_DYNATRACE_PLATFORM_TOKENfor tracePlatform token, sent as Bearer
envTOIL_DYNATRACE_ENVnoThe environment name --env selects this connection by, when it differs from the connection’s name

A command that needs a missing key fails with NOT_CONFIGURED naming it (“Dynatrace baseUrl not configured.”).

Environment variables (CI, or a one-off shell):

export TOIL_DYNATRACE_BASE_URL=https://dynatrace.imagile.dev
export TOIL_DYNATRACE_API_TOKEN=<your access token>
export TOIL_DYNATRACE_PLATFORM_URL=https://dynatrace-platform.imagile.dev
export TOIL_DYNATRACE_PLATFORM_TOKEN=<your platform token>

Environments

Each Dynatrace environment is one connection. --env <name> picks the connection named <name>, or the one whose env setting is <name>; an environment toil doesn’t know is an INVALID_INPUT that lists the ones it has. Without --env, the area’s default connection is used: the one named in defaults.dynatrace.connection, else the one named dynatrace, else the only one. Keys every environment shares (often platformUrl) can go once under defaults.dynatrace; a connection’s own value wins over them.

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "prod": { "area": "dynatrace", "baseUrl": "https://dynatrace.imagile.dev" },
    "staging": { "area": "dynatrace", "baseUrl": "https://dynatrace.imagile.dev/e/abc12345-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" }
  },
  "defaults": { "dynatrace": { "connection": "prod" } }
}

The tokens never go in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add prod --area dynatrace (or toil connections login prod for an existing connection) to keep them in the OS credential store, or set the env vars. TOIL_DYNATRACE_* variables configure the default connection only; for another one use TOIL_CONN_<NAME>_<KEY> (TOIL_CONN_STAGING_API_TOKEN).

toil dynatrace --env staging problems list

Commands

  • entities list: List monitored entities using an entity selector. --selector is required; --from, --to and --fields are passed through.
  • entities get: Get a monitored entity by ID (--id, plus --from, --to, --fields). data is Dynatrace’s entity as it came.
  • services: List monitored services: entities list with type("SERVICE") (--from, --to). data is { totalCount, services }.
  • workloads: List monitored Kubernetes workloads: entities list with type("CLOUD_APPLICATION") (--from, --to). data is { totalCount, workloads }.
  • problems list: List problems. --from defaults to now-2h and --to to now; --problem-selector and --entity-selector filter. data is { totalCount, problems }.
  • problems get: Get a problem by ID (--id, --fields). data is Dynatrace’s problem as it came.
  • trace: Get distributed-trace spans from Grail (--id, 16 to 32 hexadecimal characters). It runs fetch spans | filter trace.id == "<id>" | sort start_time asc and waits up to 60 seconds for Grail, polling at most once a second; past that it fails with TIMEOUT. data is the query’s result (records, types, metadata). The query sends no timeframe and no record limit, so Grail’s defaults apply: an old trace or a very large one may come back empty or cut short.

The lists fetch every page, 500 at a time, until Dynatrace stops returning a nextPageKey; totalCount is the number of items collected. They stop with an error after 1,000 pages, and like every command they’re subject to toil’s time limit (TOIL_TIMEOUT_MS, 120 s by default).

Dynatrace’s own error text isn’t shown yet: an error is the status line, such as HTTP 400 Bad Request, with toil’s fix.

toil dynatrace entities list --selector 'type("HOST"),tag("team:payments")'
toil dynatrace problems list --from now-1d --problem-selector 'status("open")'
toil dynatrace trace --id 4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736

Checking a dossier

check-dossier checks the call’s dossier for the call’s environment (--env, else the dossier’s own): each entity id it names (entity, entities) exists, through /api/v2/entities/{id}. It’s toil dynatrace check-dossier (--dossier <name|file>, or the dossier the folder resolves to), and it returns { dossier, connection, env, ok, checked, checks, unchecked }, one check per value with its key path. The CLI exits 1 when one is missing. A failure other than not-found (a bad token, an unreachable host) fails the command. Read only.

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl

    Classic environment URL, like https://<environment-id>.live.dynatrace.com (Managed: keep the /e/<environment-id> path)

    TOIL_DYNATRACE_BASE_URL

  • apiToken secret

    Access token for the classic environment API, sent as Api-Token

    TOIL_DYNATRACE_API_TOKEN

  • platformUrl

    Platform URL for trace, like https://<environment-id>.apps.dynatrace.com

    TOIL_DYNATRACE_PLATFORM_URL

  • platformToken secret

    Platform token for trace, sent as Bearer

    TOIL_DYNATRACE_PLATFORM_TOKEN

  • env

    Environment name that --env selects this connection by, when it differs from the connection name

    TOIL_DYNATRACE_ENV

Commands at a glance

  • toil dynatraceentities list

    List monitored entities using an entity selector

    MCP dynatrace_entities_list--selector <selector>--from <time>--to <time>--fields <fields>--env <name>

  • toil dynatraceentities get

    Get a monitored entity by ID

    MCP dynatrace_entities_get--id <id>--from <time>--to <time>--fields <fields>--env <name>

  • toil dynatraceservices

    List monitored services

    MCP dynatrace_services--from <time>--to <time>--env <name>

  • toil dynatraceworkloads

    List monitored Kubernetes workloads

    MCP dynatrace_workloads--from <time>--to <time>--env <name>

  • toil dynatraceproblems list

    List problems

    MCP dynatrace_problems_list--from <time>--to <time>--problem-selector <selector>--entity-selector <selector>--env <name>

  • toil dynatraceproblems get

    Get a problem by ID

    MCP dynatrace_problems_get--id <id>--fields <fields>--env <name>

  • toil dynatracetrace

    Get distributed-trace spans from Grail

    MCP dynatrace_trace--id <trace-id>--env <name>

  • toil dynatracecheck-dossier

    Check the call's dossier against Dynatrace: its entities exist

    MCP dynatrace_check_dossier--env <name>
